summary: Tiered Slack integration proxy + Confluence sync for third‑party vendor channels
description:
Issue summary:
We need a reusable, tiered Slack integration proxy plus a Confluence sync pipeline to support onboarding third-party vendor bots and webhooks without opening direct long-lived app access to core org workspaces.

Background / rationale:
- Increasing number of vendors request Slack channels and webhooks for alerts (monitoring, contract reporting, data exchanges).
- Current pattern (invite vendor app + give channel-level tokens) leads to operational churn, inconsistent retention policies, and repeated manual audits.
- Security wants short-lived credentials, central audit points, and easier offboarding. Product teams want simple channel creation templates + automated Confluence onboarding docs for vendors.

Requested outcome / scope:
1) Build a proxy layer for vendor webhooks and bot integrations that: uses short-lived service tokens issued by our central integration service, enforces channel whitelists, and can throttle/transform inbound payloads.
2) Add an automated Confluence sync: when a vendor channel is provisioned the system creates a vendor page from template, populates contact metadata, and links to SLAs and runbooks.
3) Create a lightweight Jira permission template for vendor channel owners (read-only for broad org, write for product contacts).
4) Provide a self-service web form for Product/Solutions to request vendor channels with automated approvals for low-risk partners.

Acceptance criteria:
- Proxy supports token rotation and per-channel allowlists, tested in staging.
- Confluence template page auto-created and accessible to security/relevant pods.
- Onboarding form + approval flow implemented and documented; demo to Platform leadership.
- Rollout runbook and offboarding playbook checked into Confluence.

Impact if not implemented:
- Continued manual onboarding overhead for Platform and Security teams.
- Increased audit surface and longer offboarding windows for vendor apps.

Requester notes:
- Product Ops will coordinate initial vendor pilot (3 vendors) and provide access/contact info.
- Prefer phased approach: proxy + token rotation first, then Confluence sync and form.
comments: 2026-03-04 - Aisha R.: Opening request — Product Ops wants a scalable pattern to onboard vendors with minimal security overhead. Feeding in initial vendor list in Confluence page linked above.

2026-03-05 - Platform SRE (Liam O'Connor): Acknowledged. I'll draft an architecture note for the proxy (JWT short-lived tokens + allowlist). Will scope staging POC. Assigned to myself for implementation planning.
2026-03-09 - Security (Marisol Vega): FYI — any proxy must integrate with KMS for key rotation and log every outbound message to the central audit pipeline. Also require a revocation endpoint.

2026-03-11 - Platform SRE (Liam O'Connor): POC completed in staging. Basic token issuance and allowlist working. Found payload transform edge-case for vendor X (timestamp formats). Logging to audit pipeline configured. Will schedule demo 2026-03-15.
2026-03-12 - Product Ops (Nate Brooks): Thanks — will curate pilot vendors and prepare acceptance criteria for the demo.
investigation_notes: Reviewed current vendor onboarding tickets and patterns (multiple tickets show ad-hoc channel invites and long-lived app tokens).
Built staging proxy using express/gateway + JWT signing via KMS. Token TTL 6 hours for POC; will iterate to shorter TTLs once rotation infra is finalized.
Observed vendor payload variability: detected RFC3339 vs epoch millis timestamp fields in two vendors — added normalization step in request transformer.
Confluence API rate limits observed in initial bulk-create test; added backoff and retry logic to sync pipeline.
Permissions model: created example Jira permission template for vendor-channel owners; requires one-time Jira group creation (automation will create group with naming convention vendor-<org>-owners).
risk_and_mitigation: Risks: accidental broad exposure if proxy misconfiguration or token leak. Mitigations: least-privilege allowlists, short token TTLs, audit logging, and immediate revocation endpoint plus emergency revoke playbook.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): staging proxy, token issuance, allowlist, logging. Phase 2 (1 sprint): Confluence sync + onboarding form + permission template. Phase 3: harden, rotate TTLs, pilot with 3 vendors and perform security review.
resolution: In progress — staging POC complete. Next steps: Security review and demo scheduled. Final resolution will include runbook and automation merged to infra repo.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy issues short-lived tokens and enforces channel allowlists
Confluence page auto-created from template and linked to channel
Self-service request form with approvals is available
Offboarding flow deletes tokens and tags Confluence page as archived
work_notes: Liam to create architecture note and link PRs. Need Security to sign off on KMS integration. Product Ops to provide pilot vendor contacts.
